architecture.historicalCognitionLaw: Historical cognition is derived from earlier committed WorkingSet events, not from all objects present in CAS. Materialized-but-never-selected source objects therefore have storage history but no cognition-history authority.
architecture.recallBoundary: The opt-in inspect_working_set_history cognition control returns a bounded reverse-chronological catalog of prior committed attempt identity, WorkingSet digest/event sequence and exact pins. It does not read historical source content, perform semantic search, compute embeddings/relevance, rank memories or inject sources into the current WorkingView.
architecture.agentOwnership: Harness exposes exact historical selection identities; the Agent decides when to inspect them and uses the existing AgentWorkingSetTransitionProposal to re-select any exact historical pin. Harness does not choose a recalled source on the Agent's behalf.
architecture.effectLaw: History inspection is Harness-local cognition: it performs zero Runtime dispatch and consumes zero external Tool-call budget. Its returned bytes still consume observation budget and are treated as observation-only evidence for progress accounting.
architecture.providerFaithfulness: The Provider wire uses an ordinary function-call/tool-result exchange so the model can receive a result. Exact replay therefore remains subject to structural Tool-content authority even though the payload contains only historical cognition identities.
architecture.deterministicProof: Continuity recomputes each history observation from Journal order relative to the exact committed WorkingSet that authored the Provider turn. A forged local WorkingSetHistoryReader result is rejected before the next Provider dispatch and cannot become recall authority.
architecture.schemaChange: No SQLite schema, Protocol codec, generic Memory service, semantic index, retrieval database or recommended public API was added.

behavior.recallExperiment: A deterministic run created A, then an Agent-selected successor [A,K], then a later successor [A] that explicitly dropped K. An unrelated U source was materialized in CAS but never selected. With maxToolCalls=0 the Agent called inspect_working_set_history, saw K's exact historical pin but not U, selected K through the existing WorkingSet transition, and the following WorkingView exposed A+K source content. Runtime physical dispatch and external Tool-call count both remained zero.
behavior.contentSeparation: The history observation exposed K's logical/generation/CAS identity but not K source bytes. K content became model-visible only after the Agent re-selected K into the successor committed WorkingSet. U's digest and content never appeared in the history catalog.
behavior.pagination: limit=1 returned the newest earlier committed cognition plus a nextBeforeSequence cursor; querying before that sequence returned the next older committed selection. Unselected U remained absent from every page.
behavior.cleanPause: A history function-call/result exchange followed by needs_input survived a clean fresh-process resume using the existing attempt-local cognition reconstruction path. The resumed Provider request contained the exact history transcript and Continuity Doctor remained healthy without any Runtime receipt because the result was deterministically reconstructable from Journal authority.
behavior.forgeryAttack: A deliberately forged local history reader returned an unselected U pin and fabricated current identities. The first Provider history call completed locally, but claim of the next Provider request failed with HarnessProviderCallRequestMismatch because the bound observation differed from deterministic Journal projection. The second Provider dispatch and all Runtime effects remained zero.
behavior.deepSeekWire: With request.tools empty and remaining external toolCalls equal to zero, DeepSeekTurnAdapter with working_set_history=true still exposed inspect_working_set_history as a separate Harness cognition control. With the switch disabled, the same Provider call was rejected as unavailable.
behavior.realDeepSeek: Three live deepseek-v4-flash probes used maxToolCalls=0 and a current WorkingView that omitted an authoritative launch-code source K which had previously been selected and later dropped. In all probes the model first invoked inspect_working_set_history and then authored an exact WorkingSet transition re-selecting K. History results contained neither BLUE-17 source bytes nor the RED-99 materialized-but-unselected decoy. Runtime physical dispatch and external Tool-call count stayed zero. A captured live Provider wire proved requests 1-2 did not contain BLUE-17, while request 3 after K re-selection did contain BLUE-17 and still excluded RED-99.
behavior.realModelNonClosure: The live model did not reliably conclude after successful recall. It continued inspecting history and in two probes created another successor with the same pin selection; in the captured-wire probe it later reused the same successor attempt identity and was rejected as invalid model output. This is recorded as model/transition-progress behavior, not hidden or misclassified as a recall projection failure.

conclusion: P-C1.8 demonstrates that historical recall does not yet require a semantic Memory engine. Harness already has authoritative cognition history in committed WorkingSet Journal events; the missing primitive was an Agent-visible, bounded mechanical catalog of those exact historical selections. The new opt-in history cognition control exposes identities only, costs no Runtime effect or external Tool budget, is deterministically revalidated from Journal authority, survives authorized clean resume, excludes merely materialized objects, and leaves re-selection to the Agent through the existing WorkingSet transition law. Real deepseek-v4-flash independently exercised history then re-selected the correct K pin, and the captured wire proved K content appeared only after that selection. The model's later repeated history/same-selection behavior remains a separate open progress-policy problem rather than evidence for automatic Memory management.
knownLimits: Recall is run-local WorkingSet history. P-C1.8 does not provide cross-Run personal memory, global knowledge search, embeddings, semantic retrieval, relevance ranking, summary synthesis or automatic memory injection.

The catalog exposes only exact historical selection identities. The Agent/domain must already have useful logical references or other interpretation sufficient to choose which pin to re-select; Harness does not infer semantic relevance from source content.

Historical source content remains hidden until an Agent explicitly re-selects its pin. The history catalog itself cannot answer a question whose needed distinction is unavailable from historical pin identity/metadata alone.

Exact history function-call/result replay requires both model- and Tool-content authority because the Provider-faithful response is structurally a Tool message. Metadata-only/model-only Runs cannot silently recover that transcript.
Real deepseek-v4-flash successfully recalled K but repeatedly inspected history after K content became visible. P-C1.8 proves capability usability, not optimal model recall/stop policy.

Same-pin successor WorkingSet transitions with a fresh attempt identity remain legal. The live probes showed this can produce cognition churn and can reset attempt-local state; P-C1.8 deliberately does not impose a new no-op transition law without a separate first-principles experiment.

A later live probe reused the current successor attempt ID and was correctly rejected by the existing new-attempt-identity law; this does not solve same-pin churn when each redundant transition uses a fresh identity.
Structural Tool provenance remains distinct from semantic information-flow taint tracking.
No Runtime, World, Finance or Host repository was changed.
